title: Four found dead after Kedartal avalanche; search goes on for four missing, mostly from Bankura
dek: Rescuers digging by hand through up to 12 feet of snow have recovered the bodies of two sisters from Lucknow and two men. Families from West Bengal have reached Uttarkashi.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Rescue teams have recovered four bodies from the avalanche-hit Kedartal trekking route in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi district, and four people are still missing, officials said on Wednesday. Five young trekkers from West Bengal's Bankura district were among the eight people cut off on the route after heavy snow and an avalanche on 29 October.

Two bodies were recovered on Tuesday and two more on Wednesday, PTI reported. The dead are two women and two men, according to the Deccan Chronicle. The women, two sisters from Lucknow, have been identified by their family at the Uttarkashi District Hospital, the tehsildar of Bhatwadi said. The two men had not been publicly identified by Wednesday night. The Hindu reported that the four people still missing are friends from West Bengal. The Declaration could not confirm from official statements whether any of the dead are from Bengal.

## The search

A joint team of about 10 rescuers from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering is searching at Kedarkhadak, where the group had been camping. Officials said 10 to 12 feet of snow had built up after the avalanche, and because snow-clearing machines cannot reach the site, the rescuers are digging by hand, PTI reported. Helicopters are flying food and equipment from the Matli helipad, about 100 km away, and flew the bodies out from there to the district hospital for post-mortem examination.

District Magistrate Prashant Arya said an additional SDRF team was sent to the site on Wednesday with more food and supplies. Relatives of the Lucknow sisters and a relative of one of the Bengal trekkers had reached Uttarkashi, he said, and the families had asked to be kept informed in good time. The district administration said the police, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, disaster management and food supply departments were working together on the operation. The search was to resume on Thursday morning, the Deccan Chronicle reported.

## How the group was cut off

A party of 13, seven trekkers and six support staff, left Gangotri on 27 October and was due back on 29 October. Heavy snow and an avalanche that day blocked the route. On 30 October the trekking agency sent porters and guides, who cleared about 6 km of trail. Five people were later found safe, but eight remained stranded beyond Bhojkhadak: five trekkers from West Bengal, two from Uttar Pradesh and a local guide, according to officials. The official search began on 31 October.

The family of the two sisters told The Hindu they learned of the accident through social media rather than from the trekking agency. They have asked whether weather advisories were checked and whether the agency provided enough guides and emergency arrangements, and have called for an inquiry into its role. The agency's response has not been reported.

## Bengal's response

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Monday that the state government was in constant touch with the Uttarakhand government and the SDRF through its Resident Commissioner's office in New Delhi and disaster management channels. He said Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) Ajay Mukund Ranade and the Bankura Superintendent of Police had been assigned to liaise with officials in Uttarkashi. "Our administration has reached out to the distressed families in Bankura," he said.

Kedartal, a glacial lake at about 4,700 metres above sea level, is reached by a 26-km trail from Gangotri through Bhojkhadak and Kedarkhadak, with narrow, rocky high-altitude stretches. Early-winter snow often closes the route.
